pharm: Binds androgen receptors to promote nitrogen retention and protein anabolism with relatively reduced androgenic activity; the original US product was indicated for prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema
quick: Hereditary angioedema (historical US labeling): begin ~2 mg three times daily, titrate down to maintenance
May be taken with food to reduce GI upset
Caution; nephrotic-type changes reported; can cause fluid retention
Liver function, lipids, hematocrit, virilization; INR if on warfarin
summary: Stanozolol is a 17-alpha-alkylated anabolic-androgenic steroid that was approved in the US for prophylaxis of attacks of hereditary angioedema; the brand product (Winstrol) has since been discontinued in the US. It is a Schedule III controlled substance with significant hepatotoxicity, virilizing effects, and adverse lipid effects, and is widely misused for performance/physique enhancement.
indications: Prophylaxis to decrease the frequency and severity of attacks of hereditary angioedema (per the original/historical US labeling)
Product discontinued in the US; not currently marketed there

dosage.d: Initial about 2 mg three times daily; after a favorable response, reduce dose at intervals to a maintenance dose (often 2 mg daily or every other day)
dosage.t: Daily, titrated to lowest effective dose
dosage.n: Per historical US labeling; product is discontinued in the US

dosage.d: Lower weight-adjusted doses with careful titration
dosage.t: Daily during acute prophylaxis, then reduce
dosage.n: Caution: premature epiphyseal closure and virilization risk

admin: Administer orally; may take with food to reduce GI upset
Use the lowest effective dose and titrate down once a response is achieved
Monitor liver function and other parameters during therapy
As a Schedule III controlled substance, prescribe and dispense per controlled-substance regulations
moa: Stanozolol is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It binds androgen receptors to stimulate protein synthesis and nitrogen retention (anabolic effect) with a comparatively lower androgenic potency. In hereditary angioedema it increases serum levels of C1 esterase inhibitor and C4 component of complement, reducing the frequency and severity of attacks.

absolute: Known or suspected carcinoma of the prostate or male breast
Carcinoma of the breast in females with hypercalcemia (androgens may stimulate growth)
Nephrosis or the nephrotic phase of nephritis
relative: Cardiac, renal, or hepatic conditions predisposing to edema
monitor: Liver function tests; hepatic imaging if peliosis hepatis or tumor suspected
Lipid profile, hematocrit/hemoglobin, and signs of virilization
INR/prothrombin time in patients on anticoagulants

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Anabolic-androgenic steroids cause virilization of the female fetus and are teratogenic. Stanozolol should not be used in pregnant patients.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding because of the potential for serious adverse effects on the infant, including androgenic effects.
renal: Contraindicated in nephrosis or the nephrotic phase of nephritis. Stanozolol can cause fluid and sodium retention; use cautiously in patients with renal impairment or conditions predisposing to edema.
hepatic: Stanozolol is 17-alpha-alkylated and hepatotoxic. It can cause cholestatic jaundice, elevated liver enzymes, peliosis hepatis, and hepatic tumors. Avoid in patients with hepatic disease and discontinue if liver dysfunction or cholestasis develops.

major: Warfarin / oral anticoagulants - stanozolol potentiates anticoagulant effect; reduce anticoagulant dose and monitor INR closely
Hepatotoxic drugs and alcohol - additive liver injury
moderate: Insulin / oral hypoglycemics - may alter glycemic control (dose adjustment may be needed)
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset
interactions.diagnostics: May alter thyroid function tests (decreased thyroxine-binding globulin), lipids, and other laboratory values

common: Virilization in females (hirsutism, voice deepening, menstrual changes, clitoral enlargement)
Decreased HDL and increased LDL cholesterol
serious: Hepatotoxicity - cholestatic jaundice, peliosis hepatis, hepatic adenoma/carcinoma
Suppression of clotting factors and bleeding risk with anticoagulants
Testicular atrophy and oligospermia in males; gynecomastia
rare: Hypercalcemia (in immobilized patients or breast cancer)
emergency: Acute liver failure or hepatic rupture/hemorrhage (peliosis hepatis)

monitoring: Liver function tests periodically (and hepatic imaging if tumor/peliosis suspected)
Signs of virilization (females) and growth/bone age (children)
INR/prothrombin time if on anticoagulants; blood glucose in diabetics
counsel: This is an anabolic steroid and a controlled substance - take it exactly as prescribed and never share it
Avoid alcohol; report yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine, or right-upper-abdominal pain (liver problems)
Women: report deepening voice, facial hair, or menstrual changes; men: report breast tenderness
If you take a blood thinner, you will need extra INR monitoring
Do not use for muscle-building - misuse carries serious liver, heart, and hormonal risks
pk: Anabolic/androgenic effects develop over days to weeks
Orally active 17-alpha-alkylated steroid; absorbed after oral dosing
Daily oral dosing; long-term anabolic effects with continued use
Store as directed on the product packaging
pearls: Stanozolol is a Schedule III controlled anabolic-androgenic steroid; the US brand (Winstrol) is DISCONTINUED. Information here reflects historical US labeling for hereditary angioedema prophylaxis
17-alpha-alkylation makes it orally active but hepatotoxic - cholestasis, peliosis hepatis, and hepatic tumors are key risks
Contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal virilization) and in prostate/male breast cancer
Potentiates warfarin - reduce anticoagulant dose and monitor INR; also adversely affects lipids (lowers HDL)
Widely misused for performance/physique enhancement at high doses, with virilization, cardiovascular, hepatic, and psychiatric harms
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it - do not double up. Follow your clinician's instructions for this controlled medication.
overdose: There is limited information on acute overdose of stanozolol; acute toxicity is low but chronic excess causes the serious adverse effects described (hepatic, cardiovascular, hormonal). Manage overdose supportively and symptomatically, monitor liver function and electrolytes, and contact a poison control center.
